headline: Genomic foundation model embeddings and synthetic omics data pose privacy risks
label: Privacy Risks In Genomic Data
summary: Genomic foundation models and generative omics methods are now being benchmarked for privacy, with preprints reporting near-perfect embedding reconstruction…
synthesis: The common thread is empirical evaluation of privacy leakage from learned genomic representations and generated genomic data. One preprint shows that per-token embeddings from DNA foundation models (DNABERT-2, Evo 2, NTv2) permit near-perfect sequence reconstruction through model inversion. A second proposes a multi-vector framework for genomic language models that combines perplexity-based detection, canary extraction and membership inference to quantify memorization risk. A third benchmarks 11 generative methods for synthetic bulk RNA-seq across two cancer cohorts, jointly scoring utility, biological fidelity and membership inference privacy. What is new is the move from demonstrating isolated attacks toward standardized, multi-metric assessment that treats privacy as a measurable property alongside downstream utility. All three are preprints, and no item establishes deployment-level risk thresholds.
